title: स्वरान्त धातुमा रूपायक प्रत्यय जोडिँदा हुने रूपध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तन {Morphological changes in vowels when suffixes are added}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा नेपाली भाषामा प्रयुक्त स्वरान्त धातुमा रूपायक प्रत्यय जोडिँदा हुने रूपध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तनकोअध्ययन गरिएको छ । नेपाली भाषामा पाइने स्वरान्त धातुमा रूपायक प्रत्यय जोडिँदा केकस्तो रूपध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तन हुन्छ भन्ने विषयवस्तुमा अध्ययन केन्द्रित छ । प्रस्तुत लेख गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान ढाँचामा रहेको छ । लेखका लागि आवश्यक सामग्री पुस्तकालय कार्यबाट र नेपाली मातृभाषी वक्ताबाट सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । यसका साथै नेपाली भाषाको अध्ययनमा संलग्न अन्य अध्ययतासँगको परामर्श र पुस्तकालय कार्यबाट प्राप्त सामग्रीको पनि यथोचित प्रयोग गरिएको छ । ध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तनसँग सम्बद्ध सैद्धान्तिक पक्षको अध्ययनका लागि सन्धिनियमबारे चर्चा गरिएका परम्परागत व्याकरणका पुस्तक तथा रूपध्वनि विज्ञानसम्बद्ध आधुनिक भाषाविज्ञानका पुस्तकहरूलाई द्वितीयक स्रोतका रूपमा उपयोग गर्दै सामग्री सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । यसरी सङ्कलित सामग्रीलाई उदाहरणका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्दै निष्कर्ष निकाल्ने र नियम प्रतिपादन गर्ने काम गरिएकाले सामग्रीको विश्लेषण गर्न आगमन विधिकोउपयोग गरिएको छ । नेपाली भाषामा पाइने धातुहरू व्यञ्जनान्त र स्वरान्त गरी दुई किसिमका छन् । स्वरान्त धातुलाई पनि एकस्वरान्त र द्विस्वरान्त गरी दुई भागमा वर्गीकरण गर्न सकिन्छ । धातुको अन्त्यमा एउटा स्वर मात्र रहेको छ भने त्यस्ता धातुलाई एक स्वरान्त धातु भनिन्छ भने धातुका अन्त्यमा द्विस्वर भएमा त्यस्ता धातुलाई द्विस्वरान्त धातु भनिन्छ । कुनै दुई ध्वनि एकअर्काको नजिक हुँदा ध्वनि उपस्थित हुने परिवेशका कारणले ती दुई ध्वनिमध्ये कुनै एउटा ध्वनिमा वा दुवै ध्वनिमा परिवर्तन आए त्यस्तो परिवर्तनलाई रूपध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तन भनिन्छ । नेपाली भाषाका स्वरान्त धातुमा रूपायक प्रत्यय जोडिएर क्रियापद बन्दा धातु र रूपायक प्रत्ययको प्रकृति अनुसार भिन्नभिन्न किसिमको रूपध्वन्यात्मक परिवर्तन हुन्छ ।
american_english: This article examines the phonological changes that occur when the ruupayak suffix is added to vowel-final roots in the Nepali language. It focuses on studying what kind of phonological change happens when the ruupayak suffix is added to vowel-final roots in Nepali. The article is structured as a qualitative research framework. The material for the article was collected through library work and from Nepali native speakers. Additionally, consultations with other studies on Nepali language research and the appropriate use of material obtained from library work were also conducted. For the theoretical study of phonological change, traditional grammar books discussing sandhi rules and modern linguistics books on phonetics were used as secondary sources. In this way, the collected material was presented as examples, and an inductive method was used to analyze and derive conclusions. The verbs in the Nepali language are divided into two types: those ending in consonants and those ending in vowels. Vowel-final roots can be further classified into one-vowel-final and two-vowel-final roots. A root ending in only one vowel is called a one-vowel-final root, while a root ending in two vowels is called a two-vowel-final root. When two sounds are close to each other due to the environment in which they appear, a change occurs in either one of the sounds or both, and this change is called a phonological change. When the ruupayak suffix is added to vowel-final roots in the Nepali language to form verbs, different types of phonological changes occur depending on the nature of the root and the ruupayak suffix.

The study concentrates on exploring the specific phonological alterations that occur when the ruupayak affix is added to vowel-ending morphemes within the Nepali language. The article adopts a qualitative research design. Data was gathered through library research and interviews with native Nepali speakers. In addition, consultations with other Nepali language research studies and the appropriate utilisation of library-sourced material were also carried out. For the theoretical examination of phonological modification, traditional grammar texts discussing sandhi rules and modern phonetics literature were employed as secondary sources. The collected data was thus presented as examples and an inductive method was utilised for analysis and conclusion-drawing. Verbs in the Nepali language fall into two categories: those ending in consonants and those ending in vowels. Vowel-ending morphemes can themselves be categorised into single-vowel-ending and double-vowel-ending morphemes. A morpheme ending in a single vowel is termed a single-vowel-ending morpheme, while one ending in two vowels is called a double-vowel-ending morpheme. When two sounds are in close proximity due to their positional environment, a change occurs in either one sound or both, and this is referred to as a phonological change. When the ruupayak affix is added to vowel-ending morphemes in Nepali to form verbs, various phonological modifications take place depending on the characteristics of the morpheme and the ruupayak affix.
